preservedEvidenceNotes: The phenotype boundary is the defining disclosure of this preserved edge: the target identity is Persistent Depressive Disorder (Dysthymia) and NO located anchor diagnoses it - the anchors measure mixed-definition depression (38.8 percent pooled prevalence, OR 2.21) and PROMIS depressive SYMPTOMS (26.4 and 30.6 percent) - so the target's defining chronicity is unmeasured and a reviewer may prefer to re-target the evidence at depressive-disorder; that decision is left open and recorded rather than made silently. The dominant multivariate determinants in both cohorts are psychosocial (staff disrespect OR 2.35, emotional support OR 0.48, stigma adjusted b = 0.44, social isolation as mediator) rather than disease-activity variables, so the edge must not be read as evidence of a direct autoimmune-to-mood pathway. The two cohorts share one single-metropolitan-area, predominantly Black and female, skin-confined primary-CCLE recruitment base and are not independent populations. The meta-analysis itself cautions most association analyses rest on a limited number of studies. All three PMIDs are confirmed absent from data/evidence/master-sources.json and cleared source-status preflight on 2026-09-29 with zero blocking flags.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Authoring registers this relationship only as the bounded association the located cutaneous lupus literature supports, with the phenotype boundary stated first: a 2026 systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis of 25 studies reports depression as one of the commonest discoid lupus comorbidities at pooled prevalence 38.8 percent, with a significant case-control association at OR 2.21 (95 percent CI 1.71-2.85) alongside anxiety (OR 2.40, 1.40-4.11), hypothyroidism (OR 2.55, 1.79-3.61), hypertension (OR 2.22, 1.91-2.58) and cardiovascular disease (OR 3.85, 1.67-8.88), its own authors cautioning that most association analyses rest on a LIMITED NUMBER OF STUDIES (PMID 41849118); a 2019 cross-sectional analysis of a population-based cohort of 106 patients with primary chronic cutaneous lupus (predominantly Black, metropolitan Atlanta) reports moderate-to-severe depressive symptoms in 26.4 percent (PROMIS), three to five times the local general population, with multivariate determinants of perceived staff disrespect (OR 2.35, 95 percent CI 1.06-5.17) and low emotional support (OR 0.48, 0.35-0.66) rather than any disease-severity variable (PMID 30877492); and a 2022 cross-sectional path analysis of 121 patients with primary chronic cutaneous lupus reports moderate-to-severe depression in 30.6 percent with stigma associated with depression (adjusted b = 0.44, 95 percent CI 0.23-0.66) and social isolation mediating the relationship (PMID 35953237). The registered claim is the narrowest these anchors jointly permit: that discoid lupus is associated with a substantially elevated burden of depressive morbidity at the pooled prevalence and odds the anchors report, with NO anchor diagnosing persistent depressive disorder specifically and the dominant multivariate determinants being psychosocial rather than inflammatory.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation of persistent depressive disorder is established for any individual: NO located anchor diagnoses persistent depressive disorder (dysthymia) at all - the meta-analysis pools depression outcomes of mixed definition and the two cohorts measure PROMIS depressive SYMPTOMS - so the chronicity feature that defines the catalog target is carried across a phenotype boundary rather than measured; the cohort evidence places the dominant determinants in the psychosocial domain (perceived disrespect OR 2.35, emotional support OR 0.48, stigma adjusted b = 0.44, social isolation as mediator), so the located literature supports a pathway from visible scarring, dyspigmentation and healthcare experience to depressive morbidity rather than a demonstrated direct inflammatory effect on mood; both cohort analyses are cross-sectional (the second a path analysis, which cannot establish temporal order), so reverse and reciprocal readings stand; the meta-analysis itself cautions that most association analyses rest on few studies. Individual claims require independently established discoid lupus and separately diagnosed depressive disorder with documented chronicity, exclusion of systemic lupus neuropsychiatric involvement, of corticosteroid and antimalarial treatment effects, of disfigurement-related adjustment disorder and of pre-existing psychiatric history before any attribution.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: A hypothesized psychosocial-circadian pathway rather than a direct inflammatory one: visible scarring alopecia and dyspigmentation carry stigma, social withdrawal and healthcare-interaction harm (the multivariate models' dominant determinants), which sustain depressive arousal, while a systemic inflammatory contribution (interleukin and interferon-axis effects on monoaminergic signaling) remains possible especially where systemic lupus co-travels (22.0 percent pooled SLE prevalence in the same meta-analysis); whether any individual's depression runs through the visible-disease pathway, the inflammatory pathway or a shared substrate remains hypothesized until the dermatologic, systemic and psychiatric chronology is read together.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Held at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at meta-analysis and cross-sectional-cohort class with two scope boundaries carried as controlling limitations. FIRST, a TARGET-SCOPE (phenotype) DISCLOSURE in the strongest form this batch records: the catalog identity is Persistent Depressive Disorder (Dysthymia) and NO located anchor diagnoses it - the anchors measure mixed-definition depression and PROMIS depressive symptoms - so the evidence is depression-general and the target's defining chronicity is unmeasured; if this edge lands, its claim window is depressive morbidity in discoid lupus and a reviewing clinician must separately establish the persistent-depressive-disorder phenotype. SECOND, the dominant determinants in both cohorts are psychosocial (stigma, discrimination, support) rather than disease-activity variables, so the edge must not be read as evidence of a direct autoimmune-to-mood pathway. POPULATION BOUNDS: both cohorts are primary chronic cutaneous lupus (skin-confined, predominantly discoid), predominantly Black and female, in one US metropolitan area; the meta-analysis pools 25 studies of mixed design with most association analyses on few studies. The registry already carries this identity's sibling windows and depressive-disorder's very many incoming edges; no parallel-targeting pair is created because this edge targets persistent-depressive-disorder specifically.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: NO located anchor diagnoses persistent depressive disorder, so the target's defining chronicity feature is unmeasured and carried across a phenotype boundary; all designs are cross-sectional (one a path analysis) with no temporal order; the dominant multivariate determinants are psychosocial rather than disease-activity variables; the meta-analysis cautions most association analyses rest on a limited number of studies and reports moderate variability for depression prevalence in sensitivity analysis; and both cohorts are single-metropolitan-area, predominantly Black, predominantly female, skin-confined primary CCLE populations, bounding extrapolation to systemic lupus and other demographics.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Systemic lupus neuropsychiatric involvement (the meta-analysis pools 22.0 percent SLE comorbidity) rather than skin-confined discoid lupus
Corticosteroid and antimalarial treatment effects on mood
Disfigurement-related adjustment disorder rather than a depressive disorder
Pre-existing psychiatric history and social determinants (employment, insurance, support) that dominate the cohort models
Hypothyroidism comorbidity (OR 2.55 in the same meta-analysis) as an endocrine mediator of mood symptoms
